title: Safety monitoring schedule
text: Liver function tests including ALT AST and bilirubin are performed at baseline and every 8 weeks until end of treatment at week 24. Additional unscheduled testing is performed at investigator discretion where clinically indicated.

title: Adverse event reporting
text: Any clinically significant laboratory abnormality is recorded as an adverse event. Hepatic enzyme elevation above three times the upper limit of normal requires repeat testing within seven days and consideration of dechallenge.

title: Eligibility criteria
text: Adults aged 30 to 65 years with confirmed type 2 diabetes mellitus of at least six months duration. Exclusion criteria include known hepatic impairment baseline ALT above twice the upper limit of normal and concomitant hepatotoxic medication.

title: Dosing and administration
text: AYU-008 is administered as 500 mg twice daily by the oral route for 24 weeks. Dose reduction is not permitted; treatment interruption is permitted for adverse events at investigator discretion.

title: Constituent profile
text: AYU-008 is a standardised polyherbal formulation containing four constituent fractions designated C-1 through C-4. Constituent C-3 is standardised to a marker compound quantified by HPLC in each batch.

title: Hepatic safety considerations
text: Preclinical evaluation of constituent C-3 recorded transient transaminase elevation at supratherapeutic exposure in a rodent model with recovery on withdrawal. No hepatic finding was recorded for constituents C-1 C-2 or C-4.

title: Monitoring of polyherbal formulations
text: Polyherbal preparations present an attribution problem absent from single-molecule products because an observed effect cannot be assigned to a constituent without dechallenge rechallenge or batch-level analysis. Where a hepatic signal emerges constituent-level review of the batch record is indicated.

title: Terminology mapping
text: The classical term kamala denotes a jaundice-like presentation and is mapped in this system to the controlled term Jaundice. Mapping classical terminology to controlled terms is required before disproportionality analysis because unmapped synonyms fragment a signal across several terms.

title: Related formulation hepatic observation
text: A 2024 phase II trial of a related polyherbal formulation sharing constituent C-3 recorded four cases of asymptomatic transaminase elevation among 210 participants between day 38 and day 55 of exposure. All resolved on withdrawal of study medication.

title: Comparable population no hepatic finding
text: A 2025 phase II trial in adults aged 30 to 65 with type 2 diabetes mellitus enrolled 180 participants and recorded no hepatic enzyme elevation over 24 weeks of exposure. The formulation studied did not contain constituent C-3.

title: Similar indication different endpoint
text: A 2023 trial in the same indication reported gastrointestinal intolerance as the most frequent adverse event. No hepatic parameter was collected beyond baseline so the absence of a hepatic finding is not informative.

title: Timing of drug-induced transaminase elevation
text: Drug-induced hepatocellular injury most commonly presents between four and twelve weeks of exposure. Asymptomatic transaminase elevation detected on scheduled monitoring is the usual first indication; symptomatic presentation is less common and later.

title: Monitoring interval and detection
text: Where events cluster inside a monitoring interval the interval itself limits how early the pattern can be detected. Shortening the interval increases detection sensitivity at the cost of participant burden and screening volume.

title: Disproportionality is not causation
text: A proportional reporting ratio quantifies how over-represented a term is in one exposure group relative to a comparator. It is a triage statistic. It does not establish causation and is sensitive to reporting behaviour and to small case counts.

title: Dechallenge and rechallenge
text: Resolution of an abnormality on withdrawal of the suspect product supports association. Recurrence on re-exposure supports it more strongly but deliberate rechallenge is rarely justified where the initial event was serious.

title: Serious adverse event reporting timelines
provenance: Synthetic summary of a real instrument
text: A serious adverse event occurring in a clinical trial must be reported to the Ethics Committee and the licensing authority within 24 hours with a detailed narrative within 14 days. Events not meeting seriousness criteria are recorded and reported in periodic safety reporting.

title: Investigator responsibility for causality
text: Causality assessment for an adverse event is the responsibility of the investigator. Automated systems may order and present evidence but the determination of relatedness is a clinical judgement recorded by a named person.
